audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Passion plot, supper, covenant cup, dispute over greatness, Peter warning, Mount of Olives prayer, arrest, Peter denial, mocking, council.

verses.restored: The feast of Unleavened Bread, called Passover, was drawing near.

familiar.text: Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.

modern.text: Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover, was approaching,

original.text: Ἤγγιζεν δὲ ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀζύμων ἡ λεγομένη Πάσχα.

verses.restored: The chief priests and scribes were seeking how they might remove him, for they feared the people.

familiar.text: And the chief priests and scribes sought how they might kill him; for they feared the people.

modern.text: and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to put Jesus to death; for they feared the people. Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus (Matthew 26:14–16; Mark 14:10–11)

original.text: καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὸ πῶς ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν, ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν.

verses.restored: The Adversary entered into Judas called Iscariot, who was of the number of the twelve.

familiar.text: Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.

modern.text: Then Satan entered Judas Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve.

original.text: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ Σατανᾶς εἰς Ἰούδαν τὸν ⸀καλούμενον Ἰσκαριώτην, ὄντα ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τῶν δώδεκα·

verses.restored: He went away and conferred with the chief priests and officers how he might hand him over to them.

familiar.text: And he went his way, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray him unto them.

modern.text: And Judas went to discuss with the chief priests and temple officers how he might betray Jesus to them.

original.text: καὶ ἀπελθὼν συνελάλησεν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ στρατηγοῖς τὸ πῶς ⸂αὐτοῖς παραδῷ αὐτόν⸃.

verses.restored: They rejoiced and agreed to give him silver.

familiar.text: And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.

modern.text: They were delighted and agreed to give him money.

original.text: καὶ ἐχάρησαν καὶ συνέθεντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι.

verses.restored: He consented and sought a good opportunity to hand him over apart from a crowd.

familiar.text: And he promised, and sought opportunity to betray him unto them in the absence of the multitude.

modern.text: Judas consented, and began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus to them in the absence of a crowd. Preparing the Passover (Matthew 26:17–19; Mark 14:12–16)

original.text: καὶ ἐξωμολόγησεν, καὶ ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν τοῦ παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν ⸂ἄτερ ὄχλου αὐτοῖς⸃.

verses.restored: The day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover had to be sacrificed.

familiar.text: Then came the day of unleavened bread, when the passover must be killed.

modern.text: Then came the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed.

original.text: Ἦλθεν δὲ ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν ἀζύμων, ⸀ᾗ ἔδει θύεσθαι τὸ πάσχα·

verses.restored: He sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat.

familiar.text: And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare us the passover, that we may eat.

modern.text: Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare for us to eat the Passover.”

original.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην εἰπών· Πορευθέντες ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν τὸ πάσχα ἵνα φάγωμεν.

verses.restored: They said to him, Where do you want us to prepare?

familiar.text: And they said unto him, Where wilt thou that we prepare?

modern.text: “Where do You want us to prepare it?” they asked.

original.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ θέλεις ⸀ἑτοιμάσωμεν;

verses.restored: He said to them, Look, when you enter the city, a person carrying a jar of water will meet you; follow him into the house he enters.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Behold, when ye are entered into the city, there shall a man meet you, bearing a pitcher of water; follow him into the house where he entereth in.

modern.text: He answered, “When you enter the city, a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him to the house he enters,

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἰδοὺ εἰσελθόντων ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν πόλιν συναντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ⸂εἰς ἣν⸃ εἰσπορεύεται.

verses.restored: Say to the house-master, The Teacher says to you, Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?

familiar.text: And ye shall say unto the goodman of the house, The Master saith unto thee, Where is the guestchamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?

modern.text: and say to the owner of that house, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’

original.text: καὶ ἐρεῖτε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ τῆς οἰκίας· Λέγει σοι ὁ διδάσκαλος· Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμα ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;

verses.restored: He will show you a large furnished upper room; prepare there.

familiar.text: And he shall shew you a large upper room furnished: there make ready.

modern.text: And he will show you a large upper room, already furnished. Make preparations there.”

original.text: κἀκεῖνος ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον· ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε.

verses.restored: They went and found just as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.

familiar.text: And they went, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.

modern.text: So they went and found it just as Jesus had told them. And they prepared the Passover. The Last Supper (Matthew 26:20–30; Mark 14:17–26; 1 Corinthians 11:17–34)

original.text: ἀπελθόντες δὲ εὗρον καθὼς ⸀εἰρήκει αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.

verses.restored: When the hour came, he reclined, and the apostles with him.

familiar.text: And when the hour was come, he sat down, and the twelve apostles with him.

modern.text: When the hour had come, Jesus reclined at the table with His apostles.

original.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡ ὥρα, ἀνέπεσεν καὶ ⸀οἱ ἀπόστολοι σὺν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: He said to them, With desire I desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer:

modern.text: And He said to them, “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before My suffering.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα φαγεῖν μεθʼ ὑμῶν πρὸ τοῦ με παθεῖν·

verses.restored: For I say to you, I will certainly not eat it until it is fulfilled in the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: For I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.

modern.text: For I tell you that I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”

original.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ⸀ὅτι οὐ μὴ φάγω ⸀αὐτὸ ἕως ὅτου πληρωθῇ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Taking a cup, giving thanks, he said, Take this and divide it among yourselves.

familiar.text: And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and said, Take this, and divide it among yourselves:

modern.text: After taking the cup, He gave thanks and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.

original.text: καὶ δεξάμενος ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας εἶπεν· Λάβετε τοῦτο καὶ διαμερίσατε ⸂εἰς ἑαυτούς⸃·

verses.restored: For I say to you, from now on I will certainly not drink from the fruit of the vine until the reign of the Divine comes.

familiar.text: For I say unto you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God shall come.

modern.text: For I tell you that I will not drink of the fruit of the vine from now on until the kingdom of God comes.”

original.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, ⸀οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπὸ τοῦ ⸂νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ⸃ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως ⸀οὗ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἔλθῃ.

verses.restored: Taking bread, giving thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, This is my body, given for you; do this in remembrance of me.

familiar.text: And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

modern.text: And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”

original.text: καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου ⸂[τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν διδόμενον· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.

verses.restored: Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood, poured out for you.

familiar.text: Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.

modern.text: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.

original.text: ⸄καὶ τὸ ποτήριον ὡσαύτως⸅ μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐν τῷ αἵματί μου, τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐκχυννόμενον]⸃.

verses.restored: But look, the hand of the one handing me over is with me on the table.

familiar.text: But, behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table.

modern.text: Look! The hand of My betrayer is with Mine on the table.

original.text: πλὴν ἰδοὺ ἡ χεὶρ τοῦ παραδιδόντος με μετʼ ἐμοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης·

verses.restored: For the Son of Humanity goes according to what has been determined; nevertheless woe to that person through whom he is handed over.

familiar.text: And truly the Son of man goeth, as it was determined: but woe unto that man by whom he is betrayed!

modern.text: Indeed, the Son of Man will go as it has been determined, but woe to that man who betrays Him.”

original.text: ⸂ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς μὲν⸃ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ⸂κατὰ τὸ ὡρισμένον πορεύεται⸃, πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ διʼ οὗ παραδίδοται.

verses.restored: They began to discuss among themselves who of them might be about to do this.

familiar.text: And they began to enquire among themselves, which of them it was that should do this thing.

modern.text: Then they began to question among themselves which of them was going to do this. Who Is the Greatest?

original.text: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς τὸ τίς ἄρα εἴη ἐξ αὐτῶν ὁ τοῦτο μέλλων πράσσειν.

verses.restored: A dispute also arose among them about which of them seemed to be greatest.

familiar.text: And there was also a strife among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest.

modern.text: A dispute also arose among the disciples as to which of them would be considered the greatest.

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ καὶ φιλονεικία ἐν αὐτοῖς, τὸ τίς αὐτῶν δοκεῖ εἶναι μείζων.

verses.restored: He said to them, The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those exercising authority over them are called benefactors.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors.

modern.text: So Jesus declared, “The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority over them call themselves benefactors.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οἱ βασιλεῖς τῶν ἐθνῶν κυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἐξουσιάζοντες αὐτῶν εὐεργέται καλοῦνται.

verses.restored: But not so with you; rather the greater among you must become like the younger, and the leader like the one serving.

familiar.text: But ye shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.

modern.text: But you shall not be like them. Instead, the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.

original.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως, ἀλλʼ ὁ μείζων ἐν ὑμῖν ⸀γινέσθω ὡς ὁ νεώτερος, καὶ ὁ ἡγούμενος ὡς ὁ διακονῶν·

verses.restored: For who is greater, the one reclining or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining? But I am among you as the one serving.

familiar.text: For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am among you as he that serveth.

modern.text: For who is greater, the one who reclines at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as one who serves.

original.text: τίς γὰρ μείζων, ὁ ἀνακείμενος ἢ ὁ διακονῶν; οὐχὶ ὁ ἀνακείμενος; ἐγὼ δὲ ⸂ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν εἰμι⸃ ὡς ὁ διακονῶν.

verses.restored: You are the ones who have remained with me in my tests.

familiar.text: Ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations.

modern.text: You are the ones who have stood by Me in My trials.

original.text: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε οἱ διαμεμενηκότες μετʼ ἐμοῦ ἐν τοῖς πειρασμοῖς μου·

verses.restored: I appoint to you, just as my Father appointed to me, a reign,

familiar.text: And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me;

modern.text: And I bestow on you a kingdom, just as My Father has bestowed one on Me,

original.text: κἀγὼ διατίθεμαι ὑμῖν, καθὼς διέθετό μοι ὁ πατήρ μου βασιλείαν,

verses.restored: so that you may eat and drink at my table in my reign, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

familiar.text: That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

modern.text: so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial (Matthew 26:31–35; Mark 14:27–31; John 13:36–38)

original.text: ἵνα ⸀ἔσθητε καὶ πίνητε ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης μου ⸂ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ μου⸃, καὶ ⸀καθήσεσθε ἐπὶ θρόνων ⸂τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς κρίνοντες⸃ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.

verses.restored: Simon, Simon, look, the Adversary demanded to sift you all like wheat.

familiar.text: And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:

modern.text: Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift each of you like wheat.

original.text: ⸀Σίμων Σίμων, ἰδοὺ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐξῃτήσατο ὑμᾶς τοῦ σινιάσαι ὡς τὸν σῖτον·

verses.restored: But I prayed concerning you, that your trust may not fail; and you, when you have turned back, strengthen your siblings.

familiar.text: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.

modern.text: But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”

original.text: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐδεήθην περὶ σοῦ ἵνα μὴ ἐκλίπῃ ἡ πίστις σου· καὶ σύ ποτε ἐπιστρέψας ⸀στήρισον τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου.

verses.restored: He said to him, Lord, with you I am ready to go both to prison and to death.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.

modern.text: “Lord,” said Peter, “I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μετὰ σοῦ ἕτοιμός εἰμι καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ εἰς θάνατον πορεύεσθαι.

verses.restored: He said, I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not sound today until three times you deny knowing me.

familiar.text: And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.

modern.text: But Jesus replied, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Λέγω σοι, Πέτρε, οὐ ⸀φωνήσει σήμερον ἀλέκτωρ ⸀ἕως τρίς ⸂με ἀπαρνήσῃ εἰδέναι⸃.

verses.restored: He said to them, When I sent you without purse, bag, and sandals, did you lack anything? They said, Nothing.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing.

modern.text: Then Jesus asked them, “When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything?” “Nothing,” they answered.

original.text: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅτε ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς ἄτερ βαλλαντίου καὶ πήρας καὶ ὑποδημάτων, μή τινος ὑστερήσατε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οὐθενός.

verses.restored: He said to them, But now, the one having a purse, take it, likewise a bag; and the one not having, sell one's cloak and buy a sword.

familiar.text: Then said he unto them, But now, he that hath a purse, let him take it, and likewise his scrip: and he that hath no sword, let him sell his garment, and buy one.

modern.text: “Now, however,” He told them, “the one with a purse should take it, and likewise a bag; and the one without a sword should sell his cloak and buy one.

original.text: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἀλλὰ νῦν ὁ ἔχων βαλλάντιον ἀράτω, ὁμοίως καὶ πήραν, καὶ ὁ μὴ ἔχων ⸀πωλησάτω τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ καὶ ⸀ἀγορασάτω μάχαιραν.

verses.restored: For I say to you that this written thing must be completed in me: And he was counted with lawless ones. For indeed what concerns me has its completion.

familiar.text: For I say unto you, that this that is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned among the transgressors: for the things concerning me have an end.

modern.text: For I tell you that this Scripture must be fulfilled in Me: ‘And He was numbered with the transgressors.’ For what is written about Me is reaching its fulfillment.”

original.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ⸀ὅτι τοῦτο τὸ γεγραμμένον δεῖ τελεσθῆναι ἐν ἐμοί, τό· Καὶ μετὰ ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη· καὶ γὰρ ⸀τὸ περὶ ἐμοῦ τέλος ἔχει.

verses.restored: They said, Lord, look, here are two swords. He said to them, It is enough.

familiar.text: And they said, Lord, behold, here are two swords. And he said unto them, It is enough.

modern.text: So they said, “Look, Lord, here are two swords.” “That is enough,” He answered. Jesus Prays on the Mount of Olives (Matthew 26:36–46; Mark 14:32–42)

original.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Κύριε, ἰδοὺ μάχαιραι ὧδε δύο. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἱκανόν ἐστιν.

verses.restored: Going out, he went according to custom to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed him.

familiar.text: And he came out, and went, as he was wont, to the mount of Olives; and his disciples also followed him.

modern.text: Jesus went out as usual to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed Him.

original.text: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη κατὰ τὸ ἔθος εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν· ἠκολούθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ ⸀μαθηταί.

verses.restored: Arriving at the place, he said to them, Pray not to enter testing.

familiar.text: And when he was at the place, he said unto them, Pray that ye enter not into temptation.

modern.text: When He came to the place, He told them, “Pray that you will not enter into temptation.”

original.text: γενόμενος δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ τόπου εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Προσεύχεσθε μὴ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς πειρασμόν.

verses.restored: He withdrew from them about a stone's throw, knelt down, and prayed,

familiar.text: And he was withdrawn from them about a stone’s cast, and kneeled down, and prayed,

modern.text: And He withdrew about a stone’s throw beyond them, where He knelt down and prayed,

original.text: καὶ αὐτὸς ἀπεσπάσθη ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λίθου βολήν, καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύχετο

verses.restored: Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me; yet not my will, but yours happen.

familiar.text: Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.

modern.text: “Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me. Yet not My will, but Yours be done.”

original.text: λέγων· Πάτερ, εἰ βούλει ⸀παρένεγκε ⸂τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον⸃ ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ· πλὴν μὴ τὸ θέλημά μου ἀλλὰ τὸ σὸν ⸀γινέσθω.

verses.restored: [A messenger from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.]

familiar.text: And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.

modern.text: Then an angel from heaven appeared to Him and strengthened Him.

original.text: ⸂ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος ⸀ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ ἐνισχύων αὐτόν.

verses.restored: [Being in agony, he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.]

familiar.text: And being in an agony he prayed more earnestly: and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.

modern.text: And in His anguish, He prayed more earnestly, and His sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.

original.text: καὶ γενόμενος ἐν ἀγωνίᾳ ἐκτενέστερον προσηύχετο· ⸄καὶ ἐγένετο⸅ ὁ ἱδρὼς αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ θρόμβοι αἵματος καταβαίνοντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν.⸃

verses.restored: Rising from prayer, coming to the disciples, he found them sleeping from grief.

familiar.text: And when he rose up from prayer, and was come to his disciples, he found them sleeping for sorrow,

modern.text: When Jesus rose from prayer and returned to the disciples, He found them asleep, exhausted from sorrow.

original.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἀπὸ τῆς προσευχῆς ἐλθὼν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εὗρεν ⸂κοιμωμένους αὐτοὺς⸃ ἀπὸ τῆς λύπης,

verses.restored: He said to them, Why are you sleeping? Rise and pray, so that you may not enter testing.

familiar.text: And said unto them, Why sleep ye? rise and pray, lest ye enter into temptation.

modern.text: “Why are you sleeping?” He asked. “Get up and pray so that you will not enter into temptation.” The Betrayal of Jesus (Matthew 26:47–56; Mark 14:43–52; John 18:1–14)

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί καθεύδετε; ἀναστάντες προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν.

verses.restored: While he was still speaking, look, a crowd, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was going before them. He drew near to Jesus to kiss him.

familiar.text: And while he yet spake, behold a multitude, and he that was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them, and drew near unto Jesus to kiss him.

modern.text: While He was still speaking, a crowd arrived, led by the man called Judas, one of the Twelve. He approached Jesus to kiss Him.

original.text: ⸀Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ ὄχλος, καὶ ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα προήρχετο αὐτούς, καὶ ἤγγισεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ φιλῆσαι αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Judas, do you hand over the Son of Humanity with a kiss?

familiar.text: But Jesus said unto him, Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?

modern.text: But Jesus asked him, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”

original.text: ⸂Ἰησοῦς δὲ⸃ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἰούδα, φιλήματι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδως;

verses.restored: Those around him, seeing what would be, said, Lord, shall we strike with a sword?

familiar.text: When they which were about him saw what would follow, they said unto him, Lord, shall we smite with the sword?

modern.text: Those around Jesus saw what was about to happen and said, “Lord, should we strike with our swords?”

original.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν τὸ ἐσόμενον ⸀εἶπαν· Κύριε, εἰ πατάξομεν ἐν μαχαίρῃ;

verses.restored: A certain one of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.

familiar.text: And one of them smote the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.

modern.text: And one of them struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear.

original.text: καὶ ἐπάταξεν εἷς τις ἐξ αὐτῶν ⸂τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τὸν δοῦλον⸃ καὶ ἀφεῖλεν ⸂τὸ οὖς αὐτοῦ⸃ τὸ δεξιόν.

verses.restored: Jesus answered, Permit even this. Touching the ear, he healed him.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said, Suffer ye thus far. And he touched his ear, and healed him.

modern.text: But Jesus answered, “No more of this!” And He touched the man’s ear and healed him.

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἐᾶτε ἕως τούτου· καὶ ἁψάμενος τοῦ ⸀ὠτίου ἰάσατο αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Jesus said to the chief priests, officers of the temple, and elders who had come against him, Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?

familiar.text: Then Jesus said unto the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and the elders, which were come to him, Be ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves?

modern.text: Then Jesus said to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders who had come for Him, “Have you come out with swords and clubs as you would against an outlaw?

original.text: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς τοὺς παραγενομένους ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ στρατηγοὺς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ πρεσβυτέρους· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ⸀ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων;

verses.restored: Day by day, while I was with you in the temple, you did not stretch out hands against me; but this is your hour and the authority of darkness.

familiar.text: When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.

modern.text: Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on Me. But this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness.” Peter Denies Jesus (Matthew 26:69–75; Mark 14:66–72; John 18:15–18)

original.text: καθʼ ἡμέραν ὄντος μου μεθʼ ὑμῶν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ οὐκ ἐξετείνατε τὰς χεῖρας ἐπʼ ἐμέ· ἀλλʼ αὕτη ⸂ἐστὶν ὑμῶν⸃ ἡ ὥρα καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ σκότους.

verses.restored: Seizing him, they led him away and brought him into the high priest's house. Peter was following from far away.

familiar.text: Then took they him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed afar off.

modern.text: Then they seized Jesus, led Him away, and took Him into the house of the high priest. And Peter followed at a distance.

original.text: Συλλαβόντες δὲ αὐτὸν ἤγαγον καὶ ⸀εἰσήγαγον εἰς ⸂τὴν οἰκίαν⸃ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως· ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει μακρόθεν.

verses.restored: They kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat together; Peter sat among them.

familiar.text: And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.

modern.text: When those present had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them.

original.text: ⸀περιαψάντων δὲ πῦρ ἐν μέσῳ τῆς αὐλῆς καὶ ⸀συγκαθισάντων ἐκάθητο ὁ Πέτρος ⸀μέσος αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: A certain servant girl, seeing him sitting by the light and looking closely at him, said, This one also was with him.

familiar.text: But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.

modern.text: A servant girl saw him seated in the firelight and looked intently at him. “This man also was with Him,” she said.

original.text: ἰδοῦσα δὲ αὐτὸν παιδίσκη τις καθήμενον πρὸς τὸ φῶς καὶ ἀτενίσασα αὐτῷ εἶπεν· Καὶ οὗτος σὺν αὐτῷ ἦν·

verses.restored: But he denied it, saying, Woman, I do not know him.

familiar.text: And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.

modern.text: But Peter denied it. “Woman, I do not know Him,” he said.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ⸀ἠρνήσατο λέγων· ⸂Οὐκ οἶδα αὐτόν, γύναι⸃.

verses.restored: After a little while, another seeing him said, You also are one of them. But Peter said, Human one, I am not.

familiar.text: And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.

modern.text: A short time later, someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”

original.text: καὶ μετὰ βραχὺ ἕτερος ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἔφη· Καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ· ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ⸀ἔφη· Ἄνθρωπε, οὐκ εἰμί.

verses.restored: After about one hour had passed, another insisted, saying, In truth this one also was with him, for he is a Galilean.

familiar.text: And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilaean.

modern.text: About an hour later, another man insisted, “Certainly this man was with Him, for he too is a Galilean.”

original.text: καὶ διαστάσης ὡσεὶ ὥρας μιᾶς ἄλλος τις διϊσχυρίζετο λέγων· Ἐπʼ ἀληθείας καὶ οὗτος μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἦν, καὶ γὰρ Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν·

verses.restored: Peter said, Human one, I do not know what you say. Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster sounded.

familiar.text: And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.

modern.text: “Man, I do not know what you are talking about,” Peter replied. While he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Ἄνθρωπε, οὐκ οἶδα ὃ λέγεις. καὶ παραχρῆμα ἔτι λαλοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἐφώνησεν ἀλέκτωρ.

verses.restored: The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said to him, Before a rooster sounds today, you will deny me three times.

familiar.text: And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

modern.text: And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the word that the Lord had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times.”

original.text: καὶ στραφεὶς ὁ κύριος ἐνέβλεψεν τῷ Πέτρῳ, καὶ ὑπεμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τοῦ ⸀λόγου τοῦ κυρίου ὡς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι ⸀σήμερον ἀπαρνήσῃ με τρίς.

verses.restored: Going out, he wept bitterly.

familiar.text: And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.

modern.text: And he went outside and wept bitterly. The Soldiers Mock Jesus (Isaiah 50:4–11; Matthew 27:27–31; Mark 15:16–20; John 19:1–15)

original.text: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ⸀ἔξω ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς.

verses.restored: The men holding him were mocking and beating him.

familiar.text: And the men that held Jesus mocked him, and smote him.

modern.text: The men who were holding Jesus began to mock Him and beat Him.

original.text: Καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ συνέχοντες ⸀αὐτὸν ἐνέπαιζον αὐτῷ δέροντες,

verses.restored: Covering him, they were questioning him, saying, Prophesy: who is the one who struck you?

familiar.text: And when they had blindfolded him, they struck him on the face, and asked him, saying, Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?

modern.text: They blindfolded Him and kept demanding, “Prophesy! Who hit You?”

original.text: καὶ περικαλύψαντες ⸂αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτων⸃ λέγοντες· Προφήτευσον, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;

verses.restored: They spoke many other blasphemous things against him.

familiar.text: And many other things blasphemously spake they against him.

modern.text: And they said many other blasphemous things against Him. Jesus before the Sanhedrin (Matthew 26:57–68; Mark 14:53–65; John 18:19–24)

original.text: καὶ ἕτερα πολλὰ βλασφημοῦντες ἔλεγον εἰς αὐτόν.

verses.restored: When day came, the council of elders of the people gathered, both chief priests and scribes, and they led him into their council.

familiar.text: And as soon as it was day, the elders of the people and the chief priests and the scribes came together, and led him into their council, saying,

modern.text: At daybreak the council of the elders of the people, both the chief priests and scribes, met together. They led Jesus into their Sanhedrin and said,

original.text: Καὶ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, συνήχθη τὸ πρεσβυτέριον τοῦ λαοῦ, ἀρχιερεῖς ⸀τε καὶ γραμματεῖς, καὶ ⸀ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν,

verses.restored: They said, If you are the Messiah, tell us. He said to them, If I tell you, you will certainly not trust.

familiar.text: Art thou the Christ? tell us. And he said unto them, If I tell you, ye will not believe:

modern.text: “If You are the Christ, tell us.” Jesus answered, “If I tell you, you will not believe.

original.text: λέγοντες· Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός, εἰπὸν ἡμῖν. εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἐὰν ὑμῖν εἴπω οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε·

verses.restored: And if I question, you will certainly not answer.

familiar.text: And if I also ask you, ye will not answer me, nor let me go.

modern.text: And if I ask you a question, you will not answer.

original.text: ἐὰν ⸀δὲ ἐρωτήσω, οὐ μὴ ⸀ἀποκριθῆτε.

verses.restored: But from now on the Son of Humanity will be seated at the right hand of the power of the Divine.

familiar.text: Hereafter shall the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God.

modern.text: But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”

original.text: ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ⸀δὲ ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενος ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: They all said, Are you then the Son of the Divine? He said to them, You say that I am.

familiar.text: Then said they all, Art thou then the Son of God? And he said unto them, Ye say that I am.

modern.text: So they all asked, “Are You then the Son of God?” He replied, “You say that I am.”

original.text: εἶπαν δὲ πάντες· Σὺ οὖν εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ; ὁ δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔφη· Ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι.

verses.restored: They said, What further need do we have of testimony? For we ourselves heard from his mouth.

familiar.text: And they said, What need we any further witness? for we ourselves have heard of his own mouth.

modern.text: “Why do we need any more testimony?” they declared. “We have heard it for ourselves from His own lips.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τί ἔτι ⸂ἔχομεν μαρτυρίας χρείαν⸃; αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἠκούσαμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ.
